Article Title: Rahul to Amit Shah: Won’t stop demanding accountability
Article Text:
'Amit Shahji, do not think that we will stop demanding accountability...' Rahul Gandhi said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress’ Rahul Gandhi on Sunday questioned home minister Amit Shah ’s silence over alleged police brutalities against protesting students, saying he would have to answer for what happened sooner or later.“I have no options left now’ — This is exactly what a student told me in Prayagraj yesterday. Years of preparation, selling the family land, parents burdened with debt and yet, nothing to show for it,” Rahul Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X, referring to his “Chhatron ki Goonj” event on Saturday.“This is not his failure, it is the failure of a system that refused to reward his hard work,” Rahul added.Several days have passed since the students protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over alleged paper leaks called off their agitation, yet there’s not a single word from Shah on the action taken by Delhi Police against them, he said.“Amit Shahji, do not think that we will stop demanding accountability...” he said.Meanwhile, with the monsoon session of Parliament entering its final week on Monday, party general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Sunday cautioned the govt that “history should not repeat itself”, recalling that significant laws were passed during the winter session of Parliament in 2023 despite 146 MPs being under suspension.Referring to the security breach which saw two men jumping into Lok Sabha on Dec 13, 2023, Ramesh said in a post on X, “Opposition repeatedly demanded a statement from the Union Home Minister. None was forthcoming. He remained silent as he is doing now on the brutalities inflicted by the Delhi Police on protesting youth last month.”
Article Summary: Congress’ Rahul Gandhi on Sunday questioned home minister Amit Shah ’s silence over alleged police brutalities against protesting students. “I have no options left now’ — This is exactly what a student told me in Prayagraj yesterday,” Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.

Article Title: ‘Stones, shoes thrown at my car’: Mamata faces protest during visit to kin of dead TMC worker
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Sunday alleged that her car was pelted with stones after protesters intercepted her convoy while she was visiting the family of deceased Trinamool Congress worker Birju Keot in North 24 Parganas.According to Mamata, protesters raised "thief" slogans and threw water bottles and footwear."Large stones were hurled at my car by anti-social elements, right in front of the police. The attack on the vehicle was so severe that if the windows had been open, my head would have been split open. We could have all been killed."She claimed that the incident happened in front of the police and accused them of providing protection to the BJP "This happened right in front of the police. I have never seen anything like this. What is going on? The police are providing protection to the BJP," she said.Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MP Kalyan Banerjee and Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen accompanied Mamata Banerjee. They too vented their anger against the current BJP administration after facing the protests.Kalyan Banerjee said, " Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari is running his rule through the police and getting work done by the mafia."Police had to surround the former chief minister's car as it passed through the roads of Bijpur in the same district.The husband of the former Trinamool Congress Councillor of Kanchrapara Municipality in North 24 Parganas district died in police custody, the family alleged on Saturday.The deceased's name is Birju Keot. His wife Jenny Sharma Keot, the former Trinamool Councillor of Ward number 23 of Kanchrapara Municipality, alleged that her husband died after being beaten up in the jail.
Article Summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee says her car was pelted with stones after protesters intercepted her convoy. She was visiting the family of deceased Trinamool Congress worker Birju Keot in North 24 Parganas. She claimed that the incident happened in front of the police and accused them of providing protection to the BJP.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET protest crackdown, says students were forced to apologise
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi slams BJP over NEET crackdown

NEW DELHI: Standing with a group of youngsters who faced police action during the NEET protests , Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Wednesday said the ruling party is sending goons to the homes of students and forcing them to apologise, after which those apologies are being accepted by the PM.“There is no question of the youngsters apologising… I am very proud of them and what thousands of them did… They defended the Constitution and protected the idea of India and India’s future,” Rahul said.The Congress leader held a “freewheeling” discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. It included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks” at Jantar Mantar on July 20. Farah Naaz alleged that in police detention, she faced communal barbs with a cop even calling her “anti-national”. Muskan said she was being assumed to be a Muslim which makes an Indian a “fair game”, even clarifying that she is a Hindu. Nutan Toppo said a pellet gun was fired at her.The leader of opposition’s decision to meet the youngsters to 10, Janpath, for a chat further upped the ante in the “BJP vs opposition” confrontation that has jammed the ongoing monsoon session of parliament.Continuing its aggression, a large contingent of opposition MPs marched inside the Parliament complex to protest the “absence of Amit Shah from parliament” and “Ayodhya donation scam”. The group included Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Dimple Yadav, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Dharmendra Yadav, Supriya Sule, NK Premachandran, Sagarika Ghose, Amar Singh, Chowdry Mohd Ramzan, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Naseer Hussain, K Radhakrishnan.Rahul held a placard with a face riddled with pellet gun injuries and a question “who gave the order?” The members also sought statehood for J&K.Addressing the media with the youngsters, Rahul said, “They are so young and standing before the media. But the prime minister and the home minister have no courage to stand before the press."He attacked home minister Amit Shah by saying that he is responsible for the crackdown on youngsters but “he does not have the decency to come to the Parliament, and the courage to comment on what happened.”Rahul took a jibe at PM Narendra Modi for saying that he has forgiven the students.
Article Summary: The Congress leader held a “freewheeling’ discussion at his residence with a group of youngsters who participated in the protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. The group included Riya Ahir whose photo went viral after she stood in front of a police van in Mumbai and Muskan Sharma who was victim of a cop “jabbing a baton into her buttocks”

Article Title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister today
Article Text:
Three minority breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs will meet PM Modi over breakfast on Friday

KOLKATA/NEW DELHI: Three minority breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs, who are now with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and have so far refused to be a part of the BJP-led NDA, will meet PM Narendra Modi over breakfast on Friday.Murshidabad lawmakers Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahaman and Yusuf Pathan met Union minister Amit Shah on Thursday to voice concerns over SIR tribunals and the removal of loudspeakers from mosques.They have so far stayed away from two NDA meetings. The other 17 NCPI legislators, alongside six Shiv Sena MPs who support the NDA, will also meet the prime minister Friday.
Article Summary: Murshidabad lawmakers Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahaman and Yusuf Pathan met Union minister Amit Shah on Thursday. They have so far stayed away from two NDA meetings. The other 17 NCPI legislators, alongside six Shiv Sena MPs who support the NDA, will also meet the prime minister.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan sexual harassment case: Delhi court calls allegations ‘politically motivated’, fabricated
Article Text:
A Delhi court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexual harassment charges





NEW DELHI: While acquitting former BJP MP and ex-WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh , Rouse Avenue court said the allegations levelled against him appeared to be politically motivated and fabricated.The court also highlighted that the prosecution failed to prove the allegations and that the prosecution witnesses cited turned hostile during the trial, news agency ANI reported.Additional chief judicial magistrate (MP-MLA Court) Ashwani Panwar on August 3 acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Vinod Tomar in a case of alleged sexual harassment lodged on a complaint filed by women wrestlers.The judgement is not publicly available.However, it raised questions about the manner in which the allegations were levelled against the accused persons.The court noted that the allegations were levelled simultaneously by the women wrestlers, even though the alleged incidents occurred at different times and places, ANI reported.The court also noted that some of the complainants remained in touch with the accused persons even after the accusations.They invited the former WFI chief to family functions and weddings, which raised doubts about the reliability of the allegations."Despite the alleged incidents, they had maintained cordial relations with the accused, invited him to family functions and wedding ceremonies and continued to interact with him.No contemporaneous complaint was made by them or by the persons who allegedly knew of the incidents," the court observed.The court also noticed that the victims met higher authorities but did not disclose the incident to them either.The court found that the evidence of hostile witnesses, the subsequent conduct of the alleged victims, the circumstances surrounding their earlier statements and the absence of contemporaneous complaints collectively supported the defence contention that the allegations were not reliable.During the arguments, advocate Rajiv Mohan, counsel for Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, submitted that the allegations levelled against the accused were false.The court observed that the entire allegations against the accused persons were false and fabricated, made collectively at the instance of two prosecution witnesses and the coaches of Mahadev Academy, in a deep conspiracy that appeared to be politically motivated."The allegations are strikingly similar, made at the same time, at a common place, which shows prior meticulous planning against the accused persons," the court said.After considering all the documentary and other evidence, deposition of the witnesses and other material on record, the court said, "This Court has no hitch in holding that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the allegations against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.""Accordingly, the accused Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh stands acquitted of all charges under Sections 354, 354A, 506 (Part-I) of the IPC and the accused Vinod Tomar is acquitted of the charge under Section 506 (Part-I) of the IPC," the court ordered.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: A Delhi court acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexual harassment charges. The court said the allegations levelled against him appeared to be politically motivated and fabricated. The judgement is not publicly available but raised questions about the manner in which the allegations were levelled.

Article Title: Pvt vehicles banned in an around CPR Hospital till Sunday afternoon
Article Text:
Private vehicles banned in CPR Hospital

Kolhapur

:





Private vehicles have been banned in and around Chhatrapati Pramila Raje (CPR) civil hospital from Friday afternoon until Sunday afternoon, as several development works within the hospital premises are set to be inaugurated in the presence of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , deputy chief ministers and other ministers.The hospital dean issued a notification clarifying that the restrictions will not apply to emergency vehicles, and that adequate precautions have been taken to avoid any inconvenience to patients and their relatives.The hospital is located along the busy Bhausingji Road which is home to several govt establishments. Directly opposite the hospital stands the building of the Bombay High Court’s Kolhapur bench.Though the ban of private vehicles on paper was supposed to start from 12pm, the security deployment at the hospital started the enforcement from morning which caught the visitors by surprise.As a result, the road got congested and the traffic department had to deploy additional staff to regulate movement of vehicles.“The restrictions have been placed for security reasons. It is approved by the police department. The visitors are requested to cooperate,” CPR Hospital dean Dr Sadanand Bhise said.
Article Summary: Private vehicles have been banned in and around Chhatrapati Pramila Raje (CPR) civil hospital from Friday afternoon until Sunday afternoon. Several development works within the hospital premises are set to be inaugurated in the presence of chief minister Devendra Fadnavis.

Article Title: Grocer dies by suicide in Bhosari after woman allegedly threatens police complaint
Article Text:
Pune:





A 26-year-old grocer died by suicide in Bhosari after a woman customer allegedly threatened to lodge a police complaint against him, accusing him of stealing her gold earring, which she claimed had fallen at his shop.The woman allegedly took Rs 1 lakh from the victim, who was 50% disabled, and demanded an additional Rs 55,000. Unable to bear the alleged harassment, the victim jumped from the 12th floor of his residential building in Bhosari on July 27.His father lodged a complaint against the woman with the Bhosari police on Saturday. Police have registered a case against the unidentified woman under section 108 (abetment of suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).An officer from the Bhosari police said the victim ran his father’s grocery shop on Alandi Road in Bhosari. “On July 27, he jumped from the terrace of his 12-storey residential building. He recorded a video before jumping from the building,” the officer said.In the video, the victim allegedly said he was ending his life because of the woman, who he claimed was blackmailing and harassing him. According to the police, the woman had visited his shop on the pretext of purchasing a drum but did not buy anything.“The next day, she called him and claimed that her gold earring had fallen in his shop. The victim searched the entire shop but could not find the earring. The woman later returned to the shop with another person and allegedly accused him of stealing the earring and threatened to lodge a police complaint against him,” the officer added.She allegedly took Rs 1 lakh from him and demanded another Rs 55,000. In the video, the victim reportedly said he was ending his life because he could no longer bear the harassment. He also mentioned the woman’s name and the hotel where she works.“The victim’s relative took his body to Pali in Rajasthan for the last rites. After returning, his father lodged the complaint against the woman,” he added.
Article Summary: A 26-year-old grocer died by suicide in Bhosari after a woman customer allegedly threatened to lodge a police complaint against him, accusing him of stealing her gold earring. The woman allegedly took Rs 1 lakh from the victim, who was 50% disabled, and demanded an additional Rs 55,000. Unable to bear the alleged harassment, the victim jumped from the 12th floor of his residential building.

Article Title: Autorickshaw hits bike in Hudkeshwar, two injured
Article Text: Nagpur: A 25-year-old autorickshaw driver allegedly hit a bike carrying a man and his mother on Narsala main road in Hudkeshwar on August 7, leaving both with minor injuries, before fleeing.According to the complaint, Harsh Tiwari, 25, was travelling with his mother Kiran, 53, on a bike, around 9.15pm when an auto-rickshaw struck their vehicle. The impact left Harsh and his mother injured. The auto driver allegedly fled from the spot after the collision.The injured duo was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment. Based on Harsh's complaint, Hudkeshwar police lodged a case against the absconding auto driver.Hudkeshwar police are investigating the incident and efforts are underway to establish the exact circumstances behind the accident and trace the accused auto rickshaw driver.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old autorickshaw driver allegedly hit a bike carrying a man and his mother on Narsala main road in Hudkeshwar on August 7. Harsh Tiwari, 25, was travelling with his mother Kiran, 53, on a bike, around 9.15pm when an auto- rickshaw struck their vehicle. The auto driver allegedly fled from the spot after the collision.

Article Title: Gadchiroli students return after meeting Prez Murmu
Article Text: Nagpur: A batch of tribal students from Gadchiroli's govt ashram schools are back after an educational tour of Delhi, where they met President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Before they left, CM and Gadchiroli guardian minister Devendra Fadnavis had personally seen them off at the airport.The tribal development department funded the Delhi tour for 96 tribal students from govt ashram schools in Gadchiroli, Aheri and Bhamragad under district's annual tribal sub-plan. Separately, the social justice and special assistance department has sent 360 students from Gadchiroli's govt residential schools on similar tours over past 3 years, to Hyderabad and Bengaluru in last 2 years, and to Delhi this year.At Rashtrapati Bhavan, a student from Potegaon told President Murmu, "I want to become a teacher." Murmu asked the students about their villages, education and goals, and urged them to dream big and work towards their goals with persistence. The students also visited Parliament, PM Museum, National Science Centre, IIT Delhi, Jantar Mantar, Rajghat, Red Fort, Qutub Minar and National Zoological Park.ZP Gadchiroli separately runs Mission Jikitur, which takes top scorers from its scholarship exam on educational tours. A batch of these students flew to Mumbai, where they met state chief secretary and Gadchiroli guardian secretary Rajesh Aggarwal and spoke of their ambitions to become teachers, doctors, collectors and police officers.
Article Summary: 96 tribal students from govt ashram schools in Gadchiroli, Aheri and Bhamragad went to Delhi. They met President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan. The students also visited Parliament, PM Museum, National Science Centre, IIT Delhi.

Article Title: TNCC holds state-wide rally against delimitation
Article Text:
Congress rally against Delimitation Bill





Chennai: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) on Sunday held a statewide rally against the delimitation bill proposed by the Union BJP govt. TNCC chief Manickam Tagore demanded DMK to clarify its stand on the bill.Tagore who led the rally in Chennai flayed DMK for not participating in the all-party meeting for MPs, convened by chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Saturday.“It is saddening that many of the TN MPs didn’t participate in the meeting. They (DMK) are asking us why we speak about delimitation when the bill was not tabled despite knowing very well that the BJP govt would table it without any prior announcement,’’ he said addressing the rally.Congress functionaries and cadres who participated in the rally held banners with the slogans ‘Modi-Limitation’ and raised slogans against the BJP govt and delimitation.Hitting out at DMK, Tagore said the opposition party should not give ‘lame excuses’ for not participating in the meeting. “Instead, say that you (DMK MPs) didn’t want to see Vijay’s face or that you were upset because your party president was not invited,” Tagore said.He added that the BJP govt was planning to table the delimitation during the last three days of the monsoon session of Parliament.Recalling the remarks of DMK MP Kanimozhi N V N Somu that “TN’s interest was more important than friends or foes in politics”, Tagore said the DMK MP had hinted that BJP was their new friend.Meanwhile, former Union minister P Chidambaram asked the parties who skipped the delimitation meeting to clarify their stand on the proposed delimitation bill.Congress MP Karthi Chidambaram told reporters in Sivaganga that BJP govt was planning to undertake delimitation based on population, and it would be a disadvantage for TN.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) on Sunday held a statewide rally against the delimitation bill proposed by the Union BJP govt. TNCC chief Manickam Tagore demanded DMK to clarify its stand on the bill. Tagore flayed DMK for not participating in the all-party meeting for MPs, convened by chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Saturday.

Article Title: Man murders brother with help of friend near Coimbatore, arrested after mother informs cops three days later
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: Three days after her younger son murdered her elder son with the help of his friend and a day after the body was found, a 65-year-old woman walked into the PN Palayam police station in Coimbatore district and revealed the crime, which led to the arrest of the culprits.The murdered man has been identified as D Senthilkumar, 45, of Vellamadai near PN Palayam. Police arrested his younger brother, Sampathkumar, 42, and his friend, M Anandkumar, 24, of Vellamadai on murder charges.On Thursday night, Vellamadai village administrative officer (VAO) Karthik,49, alerted police about an odour emanating from a 25-foot-deep abandoned well on a piece of vacant land in Andal Nagar. Police with the help of fire and rescue services personnel retrieved a decomposed body of a man from the well.Initial investigations led police to register a case of suspicious death under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, as the identity of the victim could not be established.On Friday, Saraswathi of Andal Nagar walked into the police station and stated that a heated altercation broke out at her residence between her elder son, Senthilkumar, and her younger son, Sambathkumar, on Tuesday night (Aug 4).During the argument, Sampathkumar, along with his friend, M Anandkumar, 24, of Vellamadai, assaulted Senthilkumar and stabbed him repeatedly with a knife, killing him on the spot.After her statement, police altered it into a murder case and arrested the duo on Friday. Investigations revealed that the duo, after murdering Senthilkumar, transported his body on a two-wheeler and dumped it into the abandoned well.They were remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: A 65-year-old woman walked into the PN Palayam police station in Coimbatore district and revealed the crime, which led to the arrest of the culprits. The murdered man has been identified as D Senthilkumar, 45, of Vellamadai. Police arrested his younger brother, Sampathkumar, 42, and his friend, M Anandk Kumar, 24, on murder charges.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Man arrested for assaulting KSRTC conductor
Article Text: Kochi: Ernakulam Central Police arrested Idukki native Shibin (30) on Saturday for attacking KSRTC bus conductor Ramesh VR with a mobile phone after the latter asked him to vacate his seat as it was reserved for women. Police registered an FIR based on the complaint filed by the Ambalappuzha native, who was on duty on a super deluxe bus from Adoor to Sultan Bathery.As per the FIR, Shibin attacked Ramesh around 10.55pm on Friday. The FIR said that Shibin was occupying a seat reserved for a lady passenger. When Ramesh approached him at Ernakulam KSRTC bus stand, Shibin said he wanted to go to Cheruthoni. As the bus was headed for Bathery in Wayanad, Ramesh asked him to alight at the bus stand. An irked Shibin got down from the bus and stood in front of the vehicle. When Ramesh alighted from the bus, Shibin verbally abused him and hit him in the face with his mobile and broke the conductor’s nose.Police registered an FIR against Shibin under relevant sections of BNS for obstructing/attacking a public servant, causing grievous hurt and uttering obscene words in a public place.The bus continued its journey after another conductor replaced the injured Ramesh. Policemen, who were present at the KSRTC stand, took Shibin into custody and police recorded his arrest on Saturday. A court remanded Shibin in judicial custody later.
Article Summary: Ernakulam Central Police arrested Idukki native Shibin (30) on Saturday for attacking KSRTC bus conductor Ramesh VR with a mobile phone. Police registered an FIR based on the complaint filed by the Ambalappuzha native. Shibin verbally abused him and hit him in the face with his mobile.
